_about: N4 loop round 7: the brief of a real Opus room on "ice hockey, three against three on a frozen lake" (22 Nov 03:40), kept for the arcade-sport keep checks.

brief.rules: Three against three plus goalies on a frozen lake, the house hockey core copied: the puck is a state (loose, carried, pass, shot) with named loss causes (poked, hit, intercept, lost, bobble); carry spring, dangle loss only on sprint plus hard turn, pickup under 15 m/s clean, 15-20 bobble, pass window +0.6 m and +-100 deg with an 18 f magnet. Verbs at 60 Hz: shoot (Space, shoot clip, 4 f, wrist 24 m/s, charge up to 30 f to 32 m/s, one-timer 8 f before to 6 f after arrival fires 4 f after the take at 28.8 m/s); pass (Q, its own pass clip, a short sweep, 3 f, 18 m/s, 23 beyond 15 m, led to the mate nearest the stick); poke (E, the template poke 5/7/12 on the strike clip as a short stick jab, reach 2.3 m, +-35 deg, odds 65 / 45.5 / 26 % front / side / behind, x0.6 on a fresh cut, cooldown 40, whiff halves turning 15 f, anti ping-pong 24 / 30 f); body check (F or right button without the puck, body_check clip, 12 f wind-up, 12 f window, impulse = mass x (closing + 1.5 m/s) over stability; hit recovery 40 f, miss 20 f); dodge (Ctrl, the dodge clip, defensive side step, 3 f start, 14 f immune to checks and pokes, 16 f recovery, cooldown 45, carrier keeps the puck at 0.7 speed). Contact changes both bodies: bump (ratio under 0.4) both freeze 3 f, victim flinches 0.3, hitter rebounds at restitution 0.2; stumble (0.4+) both freeze 6 f, victim TLHit.react 0.7 and half speed, puck free from 0.7, hitter loses half his lunge; knockdown (1.0+) both freeze 10 f, TLHit.down 60-150 f, hitter recoils 1 m/s, 0.18 m shake; a dodged check whiffs, slides 1.5 m on and stays open 20 f. THE HOOK: the lake is a grid of 4 m cells (about 25 x 12) with crack stages 0-3. A stumble adds one crack to the victim's cell. A knockdown adds two to the victim's cell and one to each of its 8 neighbours, and a knockdown on a cell already at stage 2 opens a hole at once. Cracks never heal by themselves, so the lake gets worse each period. Stage 3 opens a 2.5 m hole of black water (splash, crack sound, 0.3 m shake, 12 f freeze on everyone touching it). Expected rate from the house game's 2.7-4.9 hits a minute per side (about 7 a minute both sides, a third of them knockdowns): about 1 hole in period one, 2 in period two, 3 in period three; the bot metric holes_per_period must read at least 1 in every period, tuned by the dial cracks_per_stumble. A skater whose centre enters a hole, standing or sliding down, sinks for 180 f (3 s) and returns at his blue line edge: his side plays two against three. A puck entering a hole is lost and drops at center ice after 90 f. Holes refreeze to thin ice (stage 2) after 25 s, so the next knockdown there reopens them; at most four holes at once, none within 6 m of a crease. Match: first to 5, or three periods of 60 s with 2 s between; on fire after three straight goals (each check adds one extra crack) until the other side scores; a side trailing by two gets a lit lantern on its bench and its goals refreeze every hole in its own zone, visible to both. Intensity: a calm first period with few cracks, waves of holes and refreezes, the last 20 s of period three count every crack twice, then sudden death on rotten ice (every cracked cell one stage worse). First minute: a drill with the puck at your stick and an open net, then a rookie Bear who checks slowly. End screen: WIN or LOSE, the score, the cause that beat you with counts, one tip, the next team on the ladder; R restarts in 2 s.
brief.ai: The house brains copied: decide every 15 f staggered and at once on events, from state reaction frames old; carrier utility SHOOT, PASS, CARRY, PROTECT, DUMP with vetoes; roles F1/F2/F3 and D1/D2/D3 by time to the puck; your mates at 5 f. New hole sense: a check scores +0.25 when the victim is within 3 m of a hole or a stage-2 cell; carriers penalise lanes over holes and thin ice. Rival teams, a ladder at rookie (18 f, 6 deg, 0.08), pro (12, 4, 0.05) and all-star (7, 2.5, 0.03): 1) Millpond Bears, bulky (body_scale 2.5, fur hats, brown kit); habit: their D1 Borje lines up a body check from 6 m, telegraphed by a shoulder drop and a straight glide 24 f before contact; defence absorbs (stability x1.4, bumps where others stumble), but they turn slowly, so dodges beat them. 2) Hollow Reach Pikes, slim with long sticks and green scarves; habit: they never check and poke in pairs, telegraphed by a stick tap on the ice 20 f before each poke; defence is the stick, so a hard pass or a check beats them. 3) Northdeep Wolves, grey masks; habit: two skaters herd the carrier toward a hole, telegraphed by a wide skate and a stick raise 24 f before the second man checks; defence avoids: they dodge your checks near water (dodge clip). Reactions: on a goal they cheer (cheer clip), on swallowing a skater they taunt (taunt clip), on conceding they slump and skate a slow circle for 40 f, never idle past 2 s. Harder tiers react faster, read lanes better, hide less of the telegraph glide (24 to 20 f) and team up on herding; speeds, mass of a given team and puck physics never change by tier.
brief.controls: skate: W A S D (the cursor on the ice aims the stick). sprint: hold Shift, ten-step stamina bar. shoot: Space or left button, tap for a wrist shot, hold to charge, press as a pass arrives for a one-timer. pass_or_check: Q or right button, with the puck a led pass to the mate nearest the stick, without it a body check (F as well). poke: E, a stick jab at the carrier's puck. dodge: Ctrl, a side step away from the nearest checker, 14 f immune. Meta: R plays again, Enter skips the drill, V the whole-lake view, Esc quits.
brief.arena: A frozen mountain lake: the house hockey rink (TLKit rink, the house game's size, ice at y = 0.05) laid over a pond part, boarded by 0.8 m snowbanks instead of glass, the house goals at each end, a dark pine shore, two log cabins, a watch tower and a scoreboard placed only beyond the far side so nothing sits between the lens and the ice. Under the rink a 4 m grid of ice cells (about 25 x 12) holds crack stages, drawn as thin flat TLBodies.make plates: white hairlines, grey webs, then a 2.5 m disk of pond water with a splash ring; refrozen cells show pale blue thin ice. A knockdown's crack web spreads visibly over its 8 neighbours. Holes move the lanes every period: about 1, 2 and 3 open in periods one to three. Camera: TLCameras.chase behind the player's skater, distance 15 m, height 10 m (about 34 deg down), look_height 1, fov 58, use_velocity, avoid_space on the pack space, framed at 0.22 of the frame height with TLCameras.frame so the goal attacked and nearby holes are in view; V switches to a fixed whole-lake view for captures (TLCameras.set_subject on the player).
